A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VISTA research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and prompt templates, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across eight models and four benchmarks, human annotations of 888 claims, and FaithDial ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds CoCoNot abstention and RGM-Contradictions evaluations, confusion matrices, and error analyses.

M1.justification: v3 adds an optional fourth prompting stage that uses GPT-5 or DeepSeek V3.2 to check turn-level contradictions against full conversation history (Section 7.2; Appendix A.1.4). This is a targeted procedural extension; the original decomposition, verification, categorization, and memory pipeline remains.

E1.justification: v3 adds CoCoNot refusal detection without retrieved documents or dialogue history and RGM-Contradictions evaluation of conversational inconsistency without retrieval. These substantially broaden the tested scenarios beyond the retained four grounded-dialogue benchmarks. Appendix G also identifies non-English items within the CoCoNot evaluation.

E2.justification: FActScore and LLM-as-Judge remain the comparators on the four original benchmarks. The new RGM comparison includes a 50% random baseline alongside LLM-as-Judge (v3 Table 5). The expanded FActScore-lite description documents the previously described turn-level adaptation rather than establishing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Section 7 introduces two balanced evaluations with 250 examples per class. CoCoNot excludes Incomplete and Indeterminate categories, supplies empty reference/history inputs, and evaluates abstention specifically. RGM adds contradiction-focused accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 reporting, including DeepSeek V3.2 and low-reasoning GPT-5 configurations.

E4.justification: v3 adds per-model category confusion matrices, detailed CoCoNot false-positive and false-negative analyses with examples, and an investigation of reasoning models on contradiction detection. The original FaithDial component ablations remain unchanged; the earlier annotation-discrepancy analysis and Chainsmokers example are retained in relocated appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly states that each experiment uses one evaluation pass without averaging across seeds and explains decoding determinism. This is additional run-count disclosure, not evidence that run counts changed. Existing McNemar tests and inter-annotator agreement statistics are retained.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, human-classification, and ablation scores are retained. New results include 90.6% CoCoNot accuracy and substantial contradiction weaknesses: GPT-5 (LR) scores 54.20% accuracy with VISTA versus 89.40% with LLM-as-Judge (v3 Table 5). Appendices F–G add detailed result counts. The erroneous Llama-70B/BEGIN significance marker against LLM-as-Judge is removed, while its underlying paired-test result remains unchanged.

T1.justification: No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The quadratic equation appearing in v3 Appendix G belongs to a quoted dataset response, not the paper's theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: sequential claim-level factuality assessment, differentiated claim categories, improvements across four benchmarks and eight models, and the human-annotated dataset. The rewritten conclusion foregrounds ablation interpretations already present in v1 rather than establishing a different core claim.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies contradiction detection, explaining how decomposition can obscure discourse cues and explicitly acknowledging that verification lacks full dialogue history. It adds an overthinking hypothesis for reasoning models and interpretations of partial abstentions, extraction failures, and CoCoNot annotation problems. These are substantive applicability and mechanism discussions beyond v1's limitations.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the repository placeholder with a concrete code/data reference and adds extensive implementation and annotation documentation: Python and libraries, 4-bit inference, decoding and reasoning settings, computational cost, baseline implementation, recruitment, and interface screenshots. These primarily disclose existing procedures. However, v1's explicit statement that each main benchmark uses 500 randomly sampled test conversations is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for CoCoNot, RGM-Contradictions, HaluEval, and reasoning-model overthinking, including an explanation for excluding HaluEval. It removes the Dinan et al. Wizard-of-Wikipedia reference. The broader positioning relative to decomposition methods and LLM judges remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses and rewrites methodology and dataset descriptions, substantially recasts the conclusion, and replaces the main Discussion section with targeted evaluations while relocating retained discussion to Appendix H. Annotation material and supplementary sections are extensively reorganized. The title also shortens VISTA Score to VISTA.

P2.justification: v3 adds the contradiction-results table, eight category confusion matrices, two abstention-analysis tables, and annotation-interface screenshots. Existing annotation tables move to Appendix D. Figure 2 is reformatted with larger labels and a revised legend, and prompt appendices change from single-column to two-column layout; Figure 1 remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1's human evaluation contained only 22 abstention and eight contradiction claims. v3's dedicated 500-item evaluations substantially strengthen scrutiny of these defining capabilities, exposing serious contradiction weaknesses alongside strong abstention accuracy. Detailed error analyses and implementation documentation improve interpretability and reproducibility. The auxiliary settings imperfectly match the intended RAG setting, and some English/RAG-only scope statements remain inconsistent, but the gains in empirical scrutiny and transparency are substantial.
